\[
  \V(B,K):=\{\Phi(\mathcal A):
       \mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_s),\quad
       1\le s\le K,\quad |A_i|\le B\text{ for all }i\}.
\]
\begin{theorem}[Counting attainable ideal sizes]\label{thm:attainable-count}
There exists an absolute integer $B_{\mathrm{cnt}}$ such that, for all integers
$B\ge B_{\mathrm{cnt}}$ and $K$ satisfying
\[
  1\le K\le\frac{(\log B)^2}{100\log\log B},
\]
one has
\[
  |\V(B,K)|\le2^{B-\sqrt B}.
\]
\end{theorem}","fileDigest":"sha256-137f3d51bc6dee4e62a4897bf4da0584cd7ff247aa6003811ff239794c295b1f"},"reason":"This is Theorem 7.1: a uniform bound on the number of ideal sizes attainable by at most K generators of size at most B, with the paper's budget constant 100 and square-root exponent saving. There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and $n_0$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $\alpha(n)\le C\growth{n}$ for every integer $n\ge n_0$;
    \item the set of integers $n\ge5$ satisfying $\alpha(n)\ge c\growth{n}$ has natural density $1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently,
\[
  \alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{n})
\]
for almost all positive integers $n$, and, for every sufficiently large $X$,
\[
  \max_{1\le n<X}\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{X}).
\]
\end{theorem}","fileDigest":"sha256-137f3d51bc6dee4e62a4897bf4da0584cd7ff247aa6003811ff239794c295b1f"},"reason":"This is the eventual universal upper bound in Theorem 1.1(i), with a positive absolute C and an eventual threshold. There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and $n_0$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $\alpha(n)\le C\growth{n}$ for every integer $n\ge n_0$;
    \item the set of integers $n\ge5$ satisfying $\alpha(n)\ge c\growth{n}$ has natural density $1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently,
\[
  \alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{n})
\]
for almost all positive integers $n$, and, for every sufficiently large $X$,
\[
  \max_{1\le n<X}\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{X}).
\]
\end{theorem}","fileDigest":"sha256-137f3d51bc6dee4e62a4897bf4da0584cd7ff247aa6003811ff239794c295b1f"},"reason":"This is Theorem 1.1(ii): for some positive absolute c, the proportion of integers 5 <= n <= N satisfying the lower bound tends to one. There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and $n_0$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $\alpha(n)\le C\growth{n}$ for every integer $n\ge n_0$;
    \item the set of integers $n\ge5$ satisfying $\alpha(n)\ge c\growth{n}$ has natural density $1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently,
\[
  \alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{n})
\]
for almost all positive integers $n$, and, for every sufficiently large $X$,
\[
  \max_{1\le n<X}\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{X}).
\]
\end{theorem}","fileDigest":"sha256-137f3d51bc6dee4e62a4897bf4da0584cd7ff247aa6003811ff239794c295b1f"},"reason":"This is the extremal consequence in Theorem 1.1, expressed by positive lower and upper constants for maximumBelow at all sufficiently large real cutoffs. There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and $n_0$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $\alpha(n)\le C\growth{n}$ for every integer $n\ge n_0$;
    \item the set of integers $n\ge5$ satisfying $\alpha(n)\ge c\growth{n}$ has natural density $1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently,
\[
  \alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{n})
\]
for almost all positive integers $n$, and, for every sufficiently large $X$,
\[
  \max_{1\le n<X}\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{X}).
\]
\end{theorem}","fileDigest":"sha256-137f3d51bc6dee4e62a4897bf4da0584cd7ff247aa6003811ff239794c295b1f"},"reason":"This is the assembled main theorem: shared positive constants for the universal upper bound, density-one lower bound and simultaneous proportions, together with the extremal consequence. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $\alpha(n)\le C\growth{n}$ for every integer $n\ge n_0$;
    \item the set of integers $n\ge5$ satisfying $\alpha(n)\ge c\growth{n}$ has natural density $1$.
\end{enumerate}

\[
  \alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{n})
\]

\[
  \max_{1\le n<X}\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{X}).
\]
